subject: ACME integration: SDK auth, routing, embeddings & prompt governance
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: ACME integration: SDK auth, routing, embeddings & prompt governance

Hi Jordan —

Great to chat earlier today — thanks for walking through Acme's goals and the initial architecture. As discussed, here's a short recap + list of technical questions so we can scope the upcoming tech deep-dive and SOW. I've looped in our SE team (Dev & Dylan) for follow-up.

Recap (what we heard):
- Primary use: support customer-facing knowledge assistants + internal search augmentation.
- Data: mixture of public docs and limited PII (customer emails).
- Latency SLO: 500ms 95p for text generation; embeddings batch jobs OK to be asynchronous.
- Favorite infra: Node backend + Python ML workers.

Integration & architecture questions (please reply inline where possible):
1) SDK / runtime: do you prefer server-side SDK usage (Node) or direct REST calls from backend? Any language preferences for our examples?
2) Auth & networking: you mentioned Okta previously — do you want OIDC-based short-lived tokens for API calls, or API keys via a VPC private deployment? Need SSO + SCIM?
3) Routing & fallback: do you need traffic pinned to a dedicated pool (predictable latency) with an automated fallback to hosted instances if capacity is constrained? Any region constraints?
4) Structured output / tool calling: do you have existing JSON schemas for actions (e.g., open-ticket, fetch-order)? Are you planning to use function/tool calls or parse model output?
5) Embeddings & reranker: which vector DB are you planning to use (Pinecone/Weaviate/Anthropic-managed)? Do you want Redwood-managed embeddings batching or self-hosted pipeline?
6) Prompt templates & governance: how would you like to version system prompts and keep an audit trail? Concerns about prompt injection / adversarial inputs?

Attachments: I've attached a short architecture overview and a prompt governance checklist for reference.

Proposed next steps:
- Please answer the questions above (2–3 bullets each).
- Tech deep-dive (60–90m) next week — proposed times below.
- SE-led implementation plan + SOW after the deep-dive.

Available times (PST): Thu 2/26 10:00–12:00, Fri 2/27 9:00–11:00 — happy to adjust.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124

Attachments: redwood-architecture-overview.pdf, prompt-governance-checklist.md
From: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir.g@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME integration: SDK auth, routing, embeddings & prompt governance

Marissa — thanks for the recap and the materials. Quick answers inline below; Samir and I will add any gaps.

1) SDK / runtime: We primarily run Node for our customer API and Python for ML jobs. Node SDK examples are high priority.

2) Auth & networking: We use Okta, prefer OIDC + short-lived tokens. For anything that touches PII we'd like VPC/private deployment or customer-managed key option. SCIM would be nice for provisioning.

3) Routing & fallback: Yes — we want predictable latency. Ideally pin to a dedicated pool in us-west with fallback to hosted but only if latency stays within SLOs.

4) Structured output / tool calling: We have some JSON action schemas for ticketing and order lookup. We'd prefer function/tool calling with schema validation enforced server-side.

5) Embeddings & reranker: We're currently evaluating Pinecone (trial) but open to other options. We'd prefer Redwood-managed batching for embeddings to simplify ops. Also need to know about vector privacy controls.

6) Prompt governance: Major concern is prompt injection from user-provided data. We need recommendations for: versioning prompts, immutable system prompts, detection of prompt injection, and a red-team plan to validate guards.

Deliverables we need from Redwood: SSO + OIDC integration checklist, example Node & Python snippets, and a proposed timeline for Private deployment (if required).

Propose tech deep-dive: Wed 3/4 10:00 PT or Thu 3/5 13:00 PT.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Hayes
CTO, Acme Corp
jordan.hayes@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME integration: SDK auth, routing, embeddings & prompt governance

Jordan — this is great, thanks for the quick answers. Looping in Dev (SE) and Dylan (Sales Engineer) to scope the tech deep-dive and SOW. Below are clarifications and our recommended approach based on what you shared.

SDK & examples
- We'll provide Node + Python SDK examples and a small reference repo showing server-side usage patterns (token refresh flows, batching embeddings job). See attached: acme-sdk-auth-snippets.txt

Auth & networking
- Recommendation: OIDC short-lived tokens for general traffic + optional mTLS for Private deployment. For data with PII we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) with CMEK (customer-managed keys) and SCIM for user provisioning. We'll include an SSO/Okta checklist in the packet.

Routing & capacity
- You can pin routes to a Dedicated pool in us-west. We can configure policy-based routing (by route or API key) with fallback to a compatible hosted model variant if capacity constrained — fallback triggered only if latency < SLO threshold. We'll document routing policies and failure modes.

Structured output & tool calling
- Redwood supports function/tool calling with strong JSON schema enforcement. We'll recommend server-side schema validation + model-level output parsing as a second defense. If you share your current schemas, Dev will map them to our function-calling examples.

Embeddings & reranker
- For embeddings: recommend rdx-embed-small model for lower cost + rdx-embed-1 for quality; Redwood-managed batching is available and we can push directly to Pinecone or your chosen vector DB. We provide encryption-at-rest options and redaction hooks for PII before indexing. For reranking we can run a lightweight cross-encoder reranker at query time — we'll provide latency/cost estimates.

Prompt templates & system prompt governance (high level)
- Versioning: keep prompt templates in a Git repo with semantic versioning (e.g., prompts/v1.2.0). Include metadata: author, change reason, evaluation set id, rollout percentage.
- Audit trail: log the active system prompt id/version with every inference request (stored in audit logs).
- Prompt injection mitigations: input sanitization, explicit instruction tokens (deny-list patterns), model-based classifier to flag adversarial inputs, and strict function-call schema enforcement.
- Red teaming: run adversarial prompt suites against staging models weekly during rollout and pre-release. Track regressions with targeted evals and blocklist patterns. We'll provide a starter red-team set and tooling recommendations.

Next steps (proposed):
- Dev to schedule a 90m tech deep-dive (architecture + security) and capture SOW scope.
- Marissa to send SOW draft and pricing guidance for Dedicated vs Private.
- Deliverables: Node/Python snippets, Okta/SCIM checklist, routing policy doc, prompt governance checklist.

Action owners & timeline:
- Dev: map schemas & prepare function-calling examples (due 3/2).
- Dylan: prepare latency/cost estimates for reranker (due 3/2).
- Marissa: draft SOW + preliminary pricing (due 3/3).

Open Qs: can you confirm Pinecone project id and whether you want Redwood-managed embeddings pipeline? Also confirm primary contact for Okta provisioning.

Thanks — we'll send the packet before the tech call.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
